summary: Describes the Russian federal standard hash function GOST R 34.11-94, for developers and users who need to compute hashes with it in Internet applications. It is informational.

eli5.summary: It explains a way to squish any message into a short fingerprint, using a method from a Russian standard.

questions: how does the gost hash function work
how long is a gost r 34.11-94 hash
is the gost hash function secure
subtitle: The Russian federal standard hash function, which turns any bit sequence into a 256-bit value.

tldr.problem: Russian cryptography was being used in Internet applications, and developers and users needed a written description of the GOST R 34.11-94 hash function.
tldr.mechanism: The function processes the message in 256-bit blocks. A step function generates keys, encrypts parts of the running hash with GOST 28147-89 in ECB mode and mixes the result with a shift register, and the final steps also fold in the length and a checksum.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5831 is an Informational description, not an IETF standard, and it was updated by RFC 6986. It estimates the function's resistance at 2^128 operations, with a known method reducing that to 2^105.

today: RFC 5831 is Informational and was updated by RFC 6986; it has not been obsoleted. The text itself makes no statement about current deployment.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
This document is a source of information about GOST R 34.11-94, the Russian Federal standard hash function and one of the Russian cryptographic standard algorithms called GOST algorithms. It was created because Russian cryptography is being used in Internet applications. It was accepted by Act 154 of 23.05.1994 of the Russian federal committee for standards.

A hash function maps an arbitrary sequence of binary symbols onto an image of fixed small length. Hashing speeds up digital signatures because only the short image of the data is actually signed. The hash function is used for signature systems based on GOST R 34.10-2001; see RFC 5832.
sections.eli5: A hash turns a long message into a short fingerprint. Signing the short fingerprint is much faster than signing the whole long message.

sections.title: Notation and Parameters
sections.content:
The standard works on binary words. V256 is the set of all 256-bit words, and the hash h maps any finite word M onto a word in V256. Words are read from right to left. Operations include concatenation (A||B), bitwise exclusive-or and an addition modulo a power of two.

The function depends on two parameters: h0, an initial hash value that is an arbitrarily fixed 256-bit word, and hUZ, the S-boxes (substitution tables) of the GOST 28147-89 cipher. The encryption E(K,A) is GOST 28147-89 in electronic codebook (ECB) mode, with a 256-bit key and a 64-bit block.
sections.eli5: The recipe has two adjustable settings: the starting value, and a table that scrambles letters. Change a setting and you get a different fingerprint.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Hash Function
sections.content:
The step function chi takes two 256-bit words and returns one. It has three parts that run in order.

  • Key generation. Four 256-bit keys K[1] to K[4] are built from the current hash H and the message block M, using exclusive-or, a fixed byte permutation P, a transformation A and constants C[2], C[3] and C[4]. C[2] and C[4] are all zeros.
  • Encryption. H is split into four 64-bit pieces, and each piece h[i] is encrypted with key K[i] using GOST 28147-89 in ECB mode, giving four pieces that form S.
  • Mixing. A shift-register transformation PSI is applied repeatedly. The result is chi(M, H) = PSI^61(H xor PSI(M xor PSI^12(S))).
sections.eli5: Each round makes four secret keys from what it already knows, uses them to scramble four pieces of the running fingerprint, then stirs everything many times so the pieces blend together.

sections.title: Hashing a Whole Message
sections.content:
The calculation procedure keeps four running values: the unhashed rest of the message, the current hash H (starting at h0), a 256-bit checksum SIGMA (starting at zero) and the processed length L (starting at zero).

While more than 256 bits remain, it takes the low-order 256-bit block M_s, sets H := chi(M_s, H), adds 256 to L and adds the block into SIGMA. Then the last, shorter piece is padded with zeros up to 256 bits, added to L and SIGMA, and three more steps follow: H := chi(M', H), then H := chi(L, H), then H := chi(SIGMA, H). The final H is the hash value h(M).

Because the length and the checksum of all blocks are fed in at the end, they are part of the result.
sections.eli5: The message is cut into equal chunks, and each chunk is stirred into the fingerprint. At the end, the message length and a running total are stirred in as well.

sections.title: Test Examples
sections.content:
Section 7 is informative. It gives a table of sixteen rows of S-box values and an all-zero initial hash value, both recommended for the test examples only. It then walks through two sample messages and lists every intermediate key, encrypted block and mixed result.

The first message is exactly 256 bits (32 bytes), so no padding is needed. The second is 400 bits (50 bytes), so it is divided into two blocks and the second, high-order block is padded with zeros. These worked values let implementers check their code step by step.
sections.eli5: The document includes worked answers, like the answer key to a math sheet, so you can check that your own version gets the same fingerprints.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The section opens by saying the entire document is about security considerations. It estimates the current cryptographic resistance of GOST R 34.11-94 at 2^128 operations of the step hash function.

It also notes a known method that reduces this estimate to 2^105 operations, but says this demands padding the colliding message with 1024 random bit blocks of 256 bits each, so it cannot be used in any practical implementation.
sections.eli5: The authors say that breaking it would take an enormous amount of work, and the one known shortcut needs a huge, odd-looking message, so it is not practical.

viz.caption: THE THREE PARTS OF THE STEP FUNCTION

items.title: Key generation
items.text: Builds four 256-bit keys from H and M.

items.title: Encryption
items.text: Encrypts four 64-bit pieces of H with GOST 28147-89 in ECB mode.

viz.caption: FINAL STEPS OF THE HASH CALCULATION (FROM RFC 5831)

data.title: Closing the hash
data.code:
H := chi (M', H)
H := chi (L, H)
H := chi (SIGMA, H)
